<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:atten}
Suppose $H_k$ and $Q_{ux,k}$ remain bounded and the block of
$\widetilde Q_{uu,k}$ associated with the remaining controls remains uniformly
nonsingular. For fixed $\sigma_j>0$, if $u_{k,j}$ approaches either of its
bounds, then
\begin{equation}
    K_{k,j:}\rightarrow0.
    \label{eq:K_zero}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Let
\begin{equation}
    d_j=[D_{b,k}]_{jj}.
\end{equation}
From \eqref{eq:Dbjj}, $d_j\rightarrow\infty$ as the corresponding slack tends
to zero. After permuting the $j$th control to the first coordinate,
\begin{equation}
    \widetilde Q_{uu,k}
    =
    \begin{bmatrix}
        d_j+\mathcal O(1) & b^\top\\
        b & C
    \end{bmatrix},
\end{equation}
where $b$ and $C^{-1}$ remain bounded. The block inverse formula therefore
gives
\begin{equation}
    e_j^\top
    \widetilde Q_{uu,k}^{-1}
    =
    \mathcal O(d_j^{-1}).
\end{equation}
Since $Q_{ux,k}$ is bounded,
\begin{equation}
    K_{k,j:}
    =
    -e_j^\top
    \widetilde Q_{uu,k}^{-1}Q_{ux,k}
    \rightarrow0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proof-1 -->
